page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne-c8d3.8xlarge is a big data and storage-focused instance designed around massive local disk capacity and balanced compute resources. The system is provisioned on the KVM hypervisor and powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, establishing a 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity operates with a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the platform does not include GPU acceleration.

A primary defining attribute of this instance is its dense bundled local storage, featuring 70,866 GB of direct-attached HDD capacity. In benchmark evaluations, CPU performance displays a distinct contrast between single-thread and parallel metrics. Single-core tests such as Geekbench (965.0) and stress-ng (1108.59) fall into the lower quartile, reflecting the modest clock speed of the Broadwell-era architecture. Conversely, multi-core throughput achieves average classification, with a PassMark CPU score of 22,938.9 and Geekbench multi-core score of 8,392.0. Large-block uncached memory operations deliver 65.79 GB/sec read and 43.6 GB/sec write throughput.

From an efficiency standpoint, the instance trades per-core execution latency for high raw storage volume and parallel throughput per infrastructure footprint. The bundled multi-terabyte HDD array avoids reliance on remote block storage network overhead for bulk data pools, though HDD mechanical latency restricts random I/O performance. This profile fits distributed big data pipelines, bulk data ingest, Apache Hadoop or Spark clusters, archival indexing, and batch map-reduce jobs requiring massive sequential disk capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne-c8d3.8xlarge is a big data instance offering 32 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor, 128.0 GB of RAM, and an integrated 70,866 GB local HDD storage pool. Built on x86_64 architecture with 20 Gbps network bandwidth and no hardware GPU accelerators, the instance delivers balanced compute density with a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Synthetic benchmarks illustrate modest single-thread performance alongside steady multi-core results, registering 23,516.82 in stress-ng multi-core and 22,938.9 in PassMark CPU tests. While uncached memory write bandwidth reaches 43.6 GB/sec, single-threaded compression tests lag due to legacy CPU clock limits. This instance provides cost-effective mass storage density and solid multithreaded capacity for Hadoop workers, sequential data processing, distributed log analytics, and large-scale batch ETL pipelines.
